name: fast_image_resize (SIMD image resizing)
baseline: image 0.25.6 resize (imageops) on the same images and filters
verdict_reason: On x86_64 it resizes 13x faster than the image crate with Lanczos3 and 22.6x faster with bilinear using AVX2, and still 4.7x faster with SIMD disabled. A separate benchmark by the zune-image author shows the same order of gap (26x on Lanczos). The image crate's unreleased next version switches to a faster resizer, which will narrow this.
tier_reason: Public criterion benchmarks with CPU, OS, rustc version and every compared crate version stated, plus a third-party run in zune-image's benchmarks.
claimed_speedup: RGB8 4928x3279 -> 852x567, ms (image vs fir avx2 / fir sse4.1 / fir rust): Lanczos3 176.09 vs 13.52 / 15.91 / 37.26; Bilinear 80.24 vs 3.55; L8 Lanczos3 116.76 vs 4.26 (13.0x, 11.1x, 4.7x; 22.6x; 27.4x) (derived from page data). Arm Neoverse-N1 RGB8 Lanczos3: image 393.06 vs fir neon 79.72 ms (4.9x) (derived from page data). zune-image benchmark, Lanczos resize: image-rs 724.4 ms vs fir 27.89 ms (26x) (derived from page data)
workload: Downscaling a 4928x3279 photo to 852x567, single-threaded, with nearest, box, bilinear, bicubic and Lanczos3 filters on RGB8, RGBA8 (with alpha premultiplication) and L8 pixels; time per resize.
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 5950X, DDR4-4000 (x86_64); Neoverse-N1 2GHz, Oracle Cloud VM.Standard.A1.Flex (ARM64)
toolchain: Rust 1.97.1, criterion 0.7.0, fast_image_resize 6.0.1; image 0.25.6, resize 0.8.9, libvips 8.15.1 single-threaded
platforms: x86_64 (SSE4.1, AVX2 with runtime detection), aarch64 NEON, wasm32 simd128, scalar fallback; no_std feature
one_liner: SIMD image resizer that downsizes 5-27x faster than the image crate's resize, depending on filter, pixel format and CPU.
how_it_is_fast: Convolution coefficients are precomputed once per row and column and applied in fixed-point integer arithmetic with SSE4.1, AVX2, NEON or simd128 kernels chosen at runtime. Resizing is done as two separable passes over contiguous rows, and alpha premultiplication is also vectorized.
use_it_when: Thumbnail and image-processing services that resize many photos, especially with Lanczos or bicubic filters.
You need correct alpha handling: it premultiplies and un-premultiplies alpha, which image 0.25 does not.
skip_it_when: You need gamma-correct resizing without extra steps: it does not convert to linear light by itself (it provides mappers for that).
Resizing is a negligible part of your pipeline compared with decoding and encoding.
caveats: Benchmarks are by the crate's author; the zune-image run is independent but on an unspecified Darwin machine.

The image crate's main branch has replaced DynamicImage resizing with the pic-scale-safe crate, which its PR describes as about 5x faster single-threaded; it is not in any release as of image 0.25.10, but once released the gap will shrink.
Speedups are largest with AVX2; on the ARM64 VM the gap over image is 4.9x.
tradeoffs: Its own image types; converting from image::DynamicImage needs the image feature or manual buffer handling.

evidence.quote: Numbers in the table mean the duration of the image resizing in milliseconds.
The `image` crate does not support multiplying and dividing by alpha channel.
This PR migrates resizing DynamicImage from the built-in resizing impl
